chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, from Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about Jihad, is it recommended (Sunnah) or obligatory (Fard)? He said: Jihad is of four types: Two are obligatory, one is recommended but is not performed except with an obligatory [context], and one is merely recommended. As for one of the two obligatory types, it is the striving of a person against his own self to avoid the sins of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and this is the greatest Jihad. And fighting those who are close to you from the disbelievers is obligatory. As for the Jihad that is recommended but is not performed except with an obligatory [context]: then fighting the enemy is obligatory upon the entire community, and if they abandon Jihad, punishment will befall them, and this is from the punishment of the community. And it is recommended for the Imam to go out with the community to fight the enemy. As for the Jihad that is merely recommended: then whatever Sunnah a person establishes and strives in its establishment, attainment, and revival, then the action and effort in it are among the best of deeds, because he has revived a Sunnah. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever establishes a good Sunnah, he has its reward and the reward of those who act upon it, without any reduction from their rewards.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four types of Jihad according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents a nuanced taxonomy of Jihad, distinguishing between individual obligatory struggle (Jihad al-Nafs) and communal obligations, while highlighting the unique status of 'reviving a Sunnah' as a distinct, highly rewarded form of Jihad. This classification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on both internal spiritual discipline and external communal defense, linking the latter to the Imam's leadership. The inclusion of the Prophet's hadith on reviving Sunnah elevates practical religious implementation to the level of major Jihadic effort.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-89 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Davood al-Minqari, on the authority of Fuzayl ibn Ayaz, “I asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), ‘Is Jihad recommended or obligatory?’

The Imam (MGB) replied, ‘There are four types of Jihad: Two types are obligatory; one type is recommended, but it is performed as obligatory; one last type is recommended. The greatest jihad is fighting yourself, trying not to commit any sins. This is obligatory. Fighting with the infidels who attack you is also obligatory. However, the third type of Jihad is fighting against the enemies and it is obligatory for all people. If they abandon it, punishment will descend upon them. This type of Jihad is recommended for the Divine Leader (MGB). At the most, the enemies attack the people, and they will fight back. However, the type of Jihad that is recommended is reviving the traditions. If you decide to establish a good tradition and make an effort in developing it, your deeds are of the best deeds, since it intends to revive the traditions.’”
